### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-core`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v12.mdx`  _(via checkProtocolCompat (symbol, a top-level function))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `040158c750c448a14fd82b39724661641d9a6837` — the merge of head `1faa38a990d9f2538af62cecd3b7f41a262c048e` into base `f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 040158c750c448a14fd82b39724661641d9a6837 && git checkout 040158c750c448a14fd82b39724661641d9a6837
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b 1faa38a990d9f2538af62cecd3b7f41a262c048e && git checkout -B drift-repro f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b && git merge --no-ff 1faa38a990d9f2538af62cecd3b7f41a262c048e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f068cde84d272d25c451003996f3752bd016001b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Request: review · area A5 · head 1faa38a990d9f2538af62cecd3b7f41a262c048e · 2026-11-14T23:34Z

Fixes #33031. Declared `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. CI green on this head (Test Core 5/8 needed one re-run for the #33508 approvals flake). After the os-dev report (comment 6885017638 on #33031), A5 added three test-pin updates that pinned the removed below-floor `migrateCommand`: runtime `app-plugin.test.ts` (now `targetMajor`, plus a module-top `@objectstack/metadata` import for check:test-source-alias) and service-package `hydration.test.ts` (`^10` to the `^16` floor). Open questions for the reviewer: is an optional `details.migrateCommand` that is now absent below the floor a narrowing (the report says no); keep the floor as a local constant held equal to the spec by a test (recommend yes).

## Review: PASS

review#2 (server area pilot) · area A5 · Fixes #33031 · head `1faa38a990d9f2538af62cecd3b7f41a262c048e` · Clause-② no. CI on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, none failing.

**What was checked** (read-only: the diff, the card, the os-dev report 6885017638 and `origin/main`):

- `checkProtocolCompat` adds `belowFloor = targetMajor !== null && targetMajor < 16`. On that arm `migrateCommand` is `undefined`, exactly as on the existing `ahead` arm, and the message names the two remedies that apply. The `null` target (`objectstack migrate meta`), the arm from the floor up to the runtime major (`--from N`) and the ahead arm are untouched.
- The remedy text is accurate. `migrate meta --from N` refuses `N < MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR` (16 on `main`, `registry.ts.template`). `--from 16` is the honest next step only once the metadata reaches 16 by another path. The code comment explains why `--from 16` is not offered as a machine-actionable substitute.
- The tests pin the floor by value against the spec: the new case sweeps every major below `runtimeMajor` and asserts that a command is withheld for exactly `0..MIGRATION_SUPPORT_FLOOR-1` and prescribed from the floor up. A release-policy move of the spec's floor therefore reds this package. The closed `details` shape test still holds five members.
- Dependent pins: `app-plugin.test.ts` now asserts `targetMajor` instead of the removed command. `hydration.test.ts` moves its fixture from `^10` to `^16`, so it keeps testing the prescribing arm.

**Rulings on the two questions:**

1. **Not a narrowing: `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.** `details.migrateCommand` was declared optional and is already absent on the ahead arm (#26480), so every reader already handles its absence. What disappears is a value that named a command known to fail, not a capability anyone could use. Nothing an author writes is refused or re-read, and the status, code and other four members are unchanged.
2. **Keep the local floor copy (agree).** It keeps the ~2.9 MB `@objectstack/spec/migrations` entry out of `metadata-core`, which reaches install doors and browser bundles. The equality test is the guard that makes a copy acceptable. The test-only import of the spec entry is fine.

**Nits (none blocking):**

- **N1:** the `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` comment for `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` lists `migrateCommand` among the members `error.details` carries without saying "when present". That was already imprecise before this PR because of the ahead arm, so it belongs on a loose-ends card, together with the platform-checklist `manifest-install-contract` wording already noted.

Nits only, so this is the final round.
